hook.line: I told y'all I was gonna start doing more tips and tricks about social media
hook.visual: Selfie-camera close-up at home, hands clasped then opening, small white title 'make your content searchable' at top and a small sentence caption at the bottom

beats.what: Promise of a social-media tip series, title states the topic
Credibility: has worked for brands with millions of followers and for small brands
Names the tip: SEO, defined as keywords for social
Why: a video must be discoverable, posting good content is not always enough
The method: type keywords on screen, with a makeup-brand example
Lists example keywords, then 'move it off the screen'
Payoff: search 'black girl makeup' and your video pops up
Nuance: TikTok sometimes picks up spoken words, but type them anyway

why_it_works: Credentials (big and small brands) come in the first 10 s, before the tip, so the advice is trusted
One concrete, hidden trick (type keywords then drag them off screen) that viewers can try on their next post
A specific worked example (a makeup brand and a real search phrase) turns the abstract 'SEO' into a picture
A fixed title at the top tells scrollers the topic even with sound off
weaknesses: 82 s in one shot with no cuts or visuals; the trick is never shown on screen
Captions are tiny (about 3% of frame height) and 86% of the text sits outside the safe area
No CTA despite promising a tip series
for_robert: Show the trick instead of only saying it: when he explains a hidden step, have Fred physically do it on screen (type the words, then drag them off the frame).
